note: Fictional companies for demonstration. Enrichment values are made up; scenarios are sample Claude output. Scores are computed live by scoring.py.

targets.acquisition_thesis: A 21-year-old grounding-products store running on plain WordPress with no email, reviews, or cart recovery: a long-tenured owner, a thin search footprint, and every standard e-commerce lever still untouched.
targets.base_case: Acquire, migrate the catalog to a modern storefront, and switch on email capture, review collection, and abandoned-cart flows. The improvement comes from conversion fixes on existing visitors rather than new traffic, so the gains are modest but low-risk.
targets.upside_case: With only 85 indexed pages, a rebuilt product and content architecture can expand the search footprint several-fold. Paired with retention email to past customers, that turns a dormant brand name into a growing organic channel.
targets.downside_case: The tiny indexed footprint may mean demand has already moved to competitors, leaving little brand equity to recover. If the owner was the main customer relationship, revenue could drop during the transition.

targets.acquisition_thesis: A 17-year-old PEMF device seller on WooCommerce that is buying paid ads while missing every retention tool, so it is paying to acquire customers it then fails to keep.
targets.base_case: Install email, cart recovery, and review collection on the current site to raise repeat purchase and conversion. This stabilizes revenue and reduces dependence on paid spend without a risky replatform in year one.
targets.upside_case: Replatform off WooCommerce and rebuild the 640-page catalog for search to shift the paid-to-organic mix. Lower acquisition cost and higher lifetime value compound into a materially more profitable business.
targets.downside_case: Paid ads may be propping up a weak organic position, so cutting spend too fast could expose a sharp revenue decline. A replatform that breaks existing URLs would compound the risk.

targets.acquisition_thesis: An established red light therapy brand with real search presence and working email, held back by an expensive-to-maintain Magento stack and no review engine.
targets.base_case: Keep the existing email program running and add review collection, which matters in a category where buyers want proof of results. Gains are incremental because the core marketing is already functional.
targets.upside_case: Migrating off Magento cuts development and hosting cost and speeds up the site, while reviews lift conversion on 2,100 already-indexed pages. The value comes from margin and conversion, not a turnaround.
targets.downside_case: This is the least distressed archaic-platform target, so the purchase price may already reflect its strengths. Magento migrations are costly and slow, and the savings could take longer than expected to appear.

targets.acquisition_thesis: A decade-old air purification retailer on a modern platform with customer-facing tools in place, but no email or cart recovery behind its paid traffic.
targets.base_case: Add email capture and abandoned-cart automation to recover revenue from the paid traffic it already buys. No replatform is needed, so execution risk is low.
targets.upside_case: A post-purchase email program built around filter replacements turns one-time device buyers into recurring customers. That recurring revenue profile would raise both margin and valuation.
targets.downside_case: Air purification is crowded with large retailers, and paid traffic suggests organic share is hard to win. Without the replacement-filter angle, the gains are limited to conversion fixes.

targets.acquisition_thesis: A young biofeedback device brand with large operational gaps but no sign of owner fatigue, which makes it more of a partnership or wholesale prospect than a near-term acquisition.
targets.base_case: If the founder is open to a deal, adding standard email, review, and cart tools would lift conversion from a low base. A three-year-old business is unlikely to be priced as a distressed asset.
targets.upside_case: An early-stage brand folded into an established catalog gains distribution and operations it lacks today. The buyer captures growth the founder could not fund alone.
targets.downside_case: A young founder is less likely to sell, and the platform could not be identified, which adds diligence uncertainty. The thin search footprint may reflect an unproven product rather than fixable neglect.

targets.acquisition_thesis: A well-run sound therapy brand on Shopify with every standard tool in place, a healthy competitor to learn from rather than a distressed target.
targets.base_case: There is little operational slack to capture: the stack, retention tools, and search presence are already strong. Any deal would be priced on current performance.
targets.upside_case: Value would have to come from catalog integration and shared fulfillment rather than fixing neglect. That is a strategic-fit argument, not the turnaround thesis this tool looks for.
targets.downside_case: Paying a full multiple for a healthy business leaves little margin for error. If integration benefits fall short, returns trail the more distressed targets on this list.
